 In His Posthumous Memoir, Eric Dane Revealed 1 Telling ALS Symptom He Didn’t Take Seriously At First
 “Some kind of weird nerve thing, I think. I shake it off,” he wrote in his posthumous memoir.
 Posted on Oct 19, 2026 UTC comment 
 Facebook 
 Pinterest 
 Link 
 by Carly Ledbetter BuzzFeed HuffPost Writer 
 Eric Dane opened up about an ALS symptom he initially dismissed in an excerpt of his posthumous memoir, published over the weekend. 
 NBC / Getty Images
 Dane died earlier this year at age 53. His book, Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments, will hit shelves in November. 
 Scott Garfield / Getty Images
 In the candid memoir, Dane talks about everything from his addiction and divorce to the symptoms that led to him figuring out he had amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, also called “ALS” or “Lou Gehrig’s disease.” 
 The Washington Post / Getty Images
 “I’m eating sushi with my kids and suddenly I can’t work the chopsticks with my right hand,” Dane says in an excerpt published exclusively in People on Sunday. “My hand tingles, and then my fingers feel numb. Some kind of weird nerve thing, I think. I shake it off. I’m probably texting too much,” he writes. “Three weeks later, it happens again, only worse. I can’t grip the chopsticks at all.” 
 Svetlana Repnitskaya / Getty Images
 The Grey’s Anatomy star previously spoke to Diane Sawyer about how the symptoms led to his eventual diagnosis. 
 Richard Foreman / Getty Images
 “So I went and saw a hand specialist, who sent me to another hand specialist. I went and saw a neurologist, and the neurologist sent me to another neurologist, who said, ‘This is way above my pay grade,’” Dane shared in the 2025 interview. 
 Ignatiev / Getty Images
 It took nine months for the actor to get a formal diagnosis, which he went public with in April 2025. He later died in February 2026 . 
 Robin L Marshall / Getty Images
 Dane is survived by his wife, actor Rebecca Gayheart, and their teenage daughters, Billie Beatrice and Georgia Geraldine. 
 Axelle/Bauer-Griffin / Getty Images
 “He spent his final days surrounded by dear friends, his devoted wife, and his two beautiful daughters, Billie and Georgia, who were the center of his world,” his family said in a statement announcing the death of the Euphoria actor. 
 Frazer Harrison / Getty Images
 “Throughout his journey with ALS, Eric became a passionate advocate for awareness and research, determined to make a difference for others facing the same fight,” they said. “He will be deeply missed, and lovingly remembered always. Eric adored his fans and is forever grateful for the outpouring of love and support he’s received.” 
 Variety / Getty Images
 This article originally appeared on HuffPost .
